text:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — ran a KV-aware prefill + adaptive-slot token-target experiment on the non-chat reranker embeddings endpoint. Seeing a surprising p95 regression and GPU kernel stalls. Posting quick notes and traces.

Ryan Cho: Can you paste the perf summary and config you used? p95/p99, model, seq len, qps?

Maya Patel: Sure, here's the pasted snippet from the smoke run:
```
Endpoint: rerank-emb-nonchat-canary
Model: open-rank-3b-quant
Traffic: 780 qps (synthetic), avg input tokens ~12
Config:
  prefill: kv-aware
  slot_target_policy: dynamic
  token_budget_target: 512 (allow up to 1024)
Observed:
  p50: 17ms  p95: 212ms  p99: 438ms
```

Elena Gomez: Those p95s are unexpectedly high for that q/s and short inputs. Any kernel selection logs? Could runtime be choosing a slower small-gemm path?

Maya Patel: Kernel profiler attached in the S3 dump — looks like ~35% of time went to the small-gemm fallback for many requests. Also saw frequent tiny batch windows (1-3 requests) during prefill.

perf-bot: Profile upload complete — s3://redwood-perf/1962003456/profiles.tar.gz :file_cabinet: :bar_chart:

Simon Li: Hypothesis: KV-aware prefill increases slot churn and creates many tiny windows -> more cache misses -> runtime opts for conservative kernels. Two quick experiments: (1) force kernel-affinity to prefer fast small-kernels, (2) raise token_budget floor (avoid sub-64 budgets) so batches don't fragment.

Ajay Singh: Ran quick iterations this afternoon:
- Run A: token_floor=128, min_batch=8 -> p95 dropped to ~95ms (single-node canary)
- Run B: kernel_affinity=small-prefer -> p95 ~80ms but end-to-end throughput fell ~12% (GPU util trade-off)

Ryan Cho: Interesting trade-off. Forcing small kernel improves latency but hurts throughput. We need an SLO-aware knob: prefer latency-sensitive flows to small kernel, let background flows use high-throughput kernels.

Maya Patel: Also uncovered a memory allocator stall during prefill: allocator fragmentation + rapid kv inserts caused ~30% stall time in the allocator thread. Filed infra bug INFR-492. Canaries with token_floor=128 + min_batch=8 + allocator-heap-fix candidate show much lower stalls.

Elena Gomez: I'll add a tracing tag for kernel_selection and kv_eviction_rate per request so we can correlate evictions -> kernel fallback -> latency. Also add a metric for slot_fill_ratio on the endpoint dashboard.

Maya Patel: Plan: canary 30% traffic tonight with token_floor=128 and min_batch=8, no forced kernel-affinity. Monitor p95 and kernel_selection tag. Roll to 100% if p95 < 120ms and kv_eviction_rate drops. Will post results here.

Ryan Cho: Good plan. If regression persists, we should run a dedicated microbenchmark that reproduces slot churn and run flamegraphs to nail down the allocator path.

Maya Patel: Agree — thanks all. I'll update once canary finishes (will include perf-bot upload of new profiles). :rocket:
